locator.text: Equation (9.1), p. 101, in the statement of Proposition 9.6

evidence: paper: \mathscr{L}_m(a,\pi) = Q^{1+h} N_{\mathrm{abs}}\,a + \mathcal{K}a + \varepsilon k^2 m^2 |n_\Phi|^2 a + ikm\,n_\Phi\pi. \tag{9.1}

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Term by term the two agree, after two encoding conventions. (1) One frequency parameter κ stands for the paper's product km: phaseFactor κ = κ·i and carrier κ Φ = exp(κ i Φ) (HarmonicCalculus.lean:68,77), so the Lean's third term ε·κ²·‖n_Φ‖²·a is the paper's εk²m²|n_Φ|²a and the Lean's fourth term phaseFactor κ · (n_Φ)_i · p is the paper's ikm n_Φ π, with the same single power of i, the same n_Φ (phaseNormal = (∂_rΦ, ∂_θΦ/R, ∂_zΦ), HarmonicCalculus.lean:189) and the same ε. (2) The prefactor Q^{1+h} on N_abs is folded into the direction field rather than written as a scalar: the Lean's first term is `along Vf a`, and along_scaled_direction (line 249) is the identity that pulls a scalar c back out, with the docstring naming c = Q^(1+h) on Nabs. At the instantiation used for the actual construction the fast direction is LinearWaveBounds.GraphDirections.fastField d n = d.fastScale n • d.fast (LinearWaveBounds.lean:112) with fastScale = ChartScales.timeCoefficient h n = Tg^(nativeIndex h n) * Q n^(1+h) (ChartScales.lean:32), i.e. Q^{1+h} times the band-pullback transfer factor the paper records for Nabs in the identity Nabs = Tg^i N_i on band pullbacks (text.txt:3323, p.63), the same pairing of Q^{1+h} with a transfer factor that the paper writes as Q^{1+h} Nabs = c_{i0} N_{i0} (text.txt:3732, p.72). The middle term matches exactly: the paper's K at (7.6) is the matrix with rows (0,−2F,0), (2F+RF_R,0,0), (G_R,0,0), and `shear` is ![-2F·a_1, (2F+R·∂_rF)·a_0, (∂_rG)·a_0], the same three entries with the same signs and the same radial derivatives. The Lean also keeps the slow part −ε∂_T outside `principal` (it sits in `remainder` via timeDirection ε Vf Vs = Vf − ε·Vs), which is what the paper does too: (9.1) holds only the principal operator, the slow transport being listed among the remaining terms.
